Wine is called שֵׁכָר because it makes drunk, שֵׁכָר יִרְדֹּפוּ (Yeshayahu 5:11), they run after strong drink; and a drink made from fruit that makes drunk carries the name as well. In יַיִן וְשֵׁכָר אַל־תֵּשְׁתְּ (Vayikra 10:9), drink no wine or strong drink, the word takes in everything that intoxicates, even what is not wine, and he brings Chazal in Nazir: one who ate pressed figs of Keilah, or drank milk or honey, and entered the Mikdash is liable.

בַּקֹּדֶשׁ הַסֵּךְ נֶסֶךְ שֵׁכָר (Bamidbar 28:7), in the holy place pour a libation of strong drink: a libation of wine that makes drunk, and it is חי, undiluted. He brings the Sifri on Pinchas, that the quarter of a hin is poured undiluted and not mixed; and the Midrash on מִיַּיִן וְשֵׁכָר יַזִּיר, where Rabbi Elazar HaKappar reads יַיִן as the mixed wine and שֵׁכָר as the undiluted, and the same proof settles it that way round and not the reverse.

אֶשְׁכָּר יַקְרִיבוּ (Tehillim 72:10), they shall bring a gift, and הֵשִׁיבוּ אֶשְׁכָּרֵךְ (Yechezkel 27:15), they brought back your gift. He glosses it a מנחה, an offering, and says the word may have four root letters.

מור.sense: The spice מֹר, myrrh, of the anointing oil and of the oil of myrrh.

more.t: מָר־דְּרוֹר (Shemos 30:23), pure myrrh, and בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמֹּר (Esther 2:12), with oil of myrrh. The Ibn Ezra reports that some explained it as musk, and holds against them that if it were musk the pasuk could not say אָרִיתִי מוֹרִי (Shir HaShirim 5:1), I have gathered my myrrh, since musk is no plant that one gathers; he takes it for a spice of the kinds that are gathered. Rabbeinu Hai explains it as the resin of a sweet-smelling tree, which he gives by its Arabic name, and on that explanation too the word may be gathered.

From Midrash Chazis, on צְרוֹר הַמּוֹר, the bundle of myrrh: as myrrh is the chief of all the spices, so Avraham Avinu is the chief of all the tzaddikim; as whoever gathers myrrh has his hands made bitter, so Avraham Avinu made himself bitter; and as myrrh gives off its scent only in fire, so Avraham Avinu made his good deeds known only in the fiery furnace.

שֹבר.sense: To consider a thing and weigh it; and a second sense, to hope, with שֵׂבֶר for hope.

more.t: וָאֱהִי שֹׂבֵר בְּחוֹמֹת יְרוּשָׁלַם (Nechemiah 2:13), and I was considering the walls of Yerushalayim: the sense is one who thinks the matter over, from the סברא, the reasoning, of Chazal's language.

In the second sense it is to hope: לֹא־יְשַׂבְּרוּ יוֹרְדֵי־בוֹר אֶל־אֲמִתֶּךָ (Yeshayahu 38:19), those who go down to the pit do not hope for Your truth; עֵינֵי כֹל אֵלֶיךָ יְשַׂבֵּרוּ (Tehillim 145:15), the eyes of all hope to You; and הֲלָהֵן תְּשַׂבֵּרְנָה (Rus 1:13), would you wait for them. The noun is שִׂבְרוֹ, his hope, at Tehillim 146:5.

שׁבר.sense: To break, whence שֵׁבֶר; מִשְׁבָּר, a breaker of the sea, and מַשְׁבֵּר, the womb; a dream's breaking open, which is its meaning; and שֶׁבֶר, grain.

more.t: וְלֹא שָׁבַר אֶת־הַחֲמוֹר (Melachim I 13:28), it did not break the donkey, and וּשְׁבָרָהּ כְּשֵׁבֶר נֵבֶל יוֹצְרִים (Yeshayahu 30:14), he shall break it as a potter's jar is broken; וְעֶצֶם לֹא תִשְׁבְּרוּ־בוֹ (Shemos 12:46), you shall not break a bone in it. The nouns are שֵׁבֶר, a breaking, as וּמִשֵּׁבֶר רוּחַ תְּיֵלִילוּ (Yeshayahu 65:14), you shall howl for breaking of spirit, and שִׁבְרוֹן, as הֵאָנַח בְּשִׁבְרוֹן מָתְנַיִם (Yechezkel 21:11), groan with breaking of loins.

אַחַת מֵהֵנָּה לֹא נִשְׁבָּרָה (Tehillim 34:21), not one of them is broken, is stressed on the earlier syllable, and is the verb in the past; רוּחַ נִשְׁבָּרָה (Tehillim 51:19), a broken spirit, is stressed on the last, and stands as a description.

כָּל־מִשְׁבָּרֶיךָ וְגַלֶּיךָ עָלַי עָבָרוּ (Yonah 2:4), all Your breakers and Your waves passed over me, is the breaking of the sea's waves in the storm; and from it, carried over, מִשְׁבְּרֵי־מָוֶת (Shmuel II 22:5), the breakers of death. עַד־הַשְּׁבָרִים (Yehoshua 7:5) is a place called by the name because they were broken there.

The womb is called מַשְׁבֵּר for the breaking of the woman in labour and her pangs: כִּי בָאוּ בָנִים עַד־מַשְׁבֵּר (Yeshayahu 37:3), the children have come to the birthstool, and כִּי־עֵת לֹא־יַעֲמֹד בְּמִשְׁבַּר בָּנִים (Hoshea 13:13). From the same he reads הַאֲנִי אַשְׁבִּיר וְלֹא אוֹלִיד (Yeshayahu 66:9), shall I bring to the birth and not deliver, as bringing the woman to that hour. And וָאֶשְׁבֹּר עָלָיו חֻקִּי he takes as cutting a covenant and decreeing a statute upon it that shall not be passed, breaking being said of a covenant here as cutting is said of one.

more.h: The breaking open of a dream
more.t: אֶת־מִסְפַּר הַחֲלוֹם וְאֶת־שִׁבְרוֹ (Shoftim 7:15), the telling of the dream and its breaking, he glosses as its interpretation: until it is interpreted the dream is like a thing sealed up, and the interpretation breaks it open and lays it bare.

more.h: Grain, and the buying of it
more.t: כִּי יֶשׁ־שֶׁבֶר בְּמִצְרָיִם (Bereishis 42:1), there is grain in Mitzrayim, and וַיִּשְׂאוּ אֶת־שִׁבְרָם (Bereishis 42:26), they loaded their grain: grain and any food. It may be called so, he suggests, because it breaks hunger, as יִשְׁבְּרוּ פְרָאִים צְמָאָם (Tehillim 104:11), the wild donkeys break their thirst. The buyer of it is himself called שׁוֹבֵר, one who breaks: לְכוּ שִׁבְרוּ וֶאֱכֹלוּ (Yeshayahu 55:1), go, buy and eat. So is the seller, וַיִּשְׁבֹּר לְמִצְרַיִם (Bereishis 41:56), he sold to Mitzrayim; and where the verb takes an object, הוּא הַמַּשְׁבִּיר לְכָל־עַם הָאָרֶץ (Bereishis 42:6), he it was who sold to all the people of the land.

עלם.sense: To be hidden, and to hide; עֶלֶם and עַלְמָה, a youth and a young woman; and עוֹלָם, a long or an everlasting time.

more.t: וְנֶעְלַם דָּבָר (Vayikra 4:13), the matter is hidden, and וְנֶעֶלְמָה מֵעֵינֵי כָל־חָי (Iyov 28:21), hidden from the eyes of all living. תְּהִי נַעֲלָמָה (Nachum 3:11) he glosses as though you had never been at all. To hide oneself is וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ מֵהֶם (Devarim 22:1), and you hide yourself from them, and to hide is אַל־תַּעְלֵם אָזְנְךָ (Eichah 3:56), do not hide Your ear.

וְאַעְלִים עֵינַי בּוֹ (Shmuel I 12:3), and I hid my eyes at him, he reads three ways: that a man took a ransom and hid his eyes from the judgment, so as not to judge as he should; or that he hid his eyes at the giver of the ransom, covering him and not uncovering his crime; and his father read it that he was ashamed to speak before the man from whom he took it, and hid his eyes from looking at him.

עֲלֻמֵנוּ לִמְאוֹר פָּנֶיךָ (Tehillim 90:8) he glosses as our errors, since a man's errors are hidden from him, and תַּעֲלֻמוֹת לֵב (Tehillim 44:22) are the heart's hidden things. So too עַל־עֲלָמוֹת שִׁיר (Tehillim 46:1), which he reads as the hidden part of the song and its secrets. Some would read וְהוּא יְנַהֲגֵנוּ עַל־מוּת (Tehillim 48:15) from hiding as well; but the Masoretic note has it as two words, עַל מוּת, and so the accurate sefarim, and then it means עַד מָוֶת, until death: He will lead us until our dying.

more.h: Whether a young woman is a virgin
more.t: וְהָיָה הָעַלְמָה הַיֹּצֵאת לִשְׁאֹב (Bereishis 24:43) is the young woman, and he holds the word covers the virgin and the one who has known a man alike, as נערה does. הִנֵּה הָעַלְמָה הָרָה (Yeshayahu 7:14) he takes of one who had known a man, the wife of the navi or the wife of his brother, and says on clear proofs that Immanuel is not Chizkiyahu. וְדֶרֶךְ גֶּבֶר בְּעַלְמָה (Mishlei 30:19) cannot be a virgin either: the things wondered at there leave no trace, the eagle's way in the sky and the snake's upon the rock, and so a man's way with an almah, where the act is not to be told; with a virgin it would be plain beyond doubt. His father brought further proofs in Sefer HaBris: were almah a virgin, there would be no עֶלֶם, a young man, formed from it, just as there is no masculine formed from בתולה, a virgin.

more.h: The youth, and why Shaul asked
more.t: בֶּן־מִי־זֶה הָעָלֶם (Shmuel I 17:56) is the youth. Shaul was not asking who he was, having already sent for him to play before him; but seeing his might as he came back from striking the Pelishti, he asked whether he was the son of a mighty man. So at בֶּן־מִי אַתָּה הַנָּעַר (Shmuel I 17:58) David understood the question, and answered with Beis HaLachmi, since Yishai was a man of war known for his might and the word carries both senses at once. Of the same sense are the days of youth, הִקְצַרְתָּ יְמֵי עֲלוּמָיו (Tehillim 89:46), You have shortened the days of his youth.

לְעֹלָם וָעֶד (Shemos 15:18), for ever and ever, and תְּשׁוּעַת עוֹלָמִים (Yeshayahu 45:17), which he reads as this world and the world to come, or else as long stretches of time, since the word is used of many days that are some part of the long עוֹלָם, world. וַעֲבָדוֹ לְעֹלָם (Shemos 21:6) is all the days until the Yovel; כִּי מֵעוֹלָם שָׁבַרְתִּי עֻלֵּךְ (Yirmiyahu 2:20) is from long ago; and לְעוֹלָם לֹא־אֶשְׁכַּח פִּקּוּדֶיךָ (Tehillim 119:93) is all the days of my life.

כפר.sense: To coat over, whence the כַּפֹּרֶת; to remove, of anger and of sin, whence atonement; and further a village, a young lion, the frost, and golden pans.

more.t: אֲכַפְּרָה פָנָיו (Bereishis 32:21), I will take away his anger; לֹא תוּכְלִי כַּפְּרָהּ (Yeshayahu 47:11), you will not be able to remove it and annul it. Atonement is this same removing: וְכִפֶּר אַהֲרֹן (Shemos 30:10), by putting the blood on the horns of the mizbeach he removes the sins of Yisrael; and so the noun יוֹם כִּפֻּרִים (Vayikra 23:28).

more.h: What Chazal show of the word
more.t: Chazal in Kesubos say מִזְבֵּחַ מזיח מכפר, the mizbeach dislodges and atones, and ask whether the two are not one thing; the answer is מזיח גזירות, it dislodges decrees, מכפר עונות, it atones for sins. Both are language of removal, since מזיח is from וְלֹא יִזַּח הַחֹשֶׁן מֵעַל הָאֵפוֹד (Shemos 28:28), the choshen shall not come loose from the ephod. In that same way they say מכפר ליה בבליתא דפרסא, he takes off the fat and wipes it away with a coarse cloth.

אִישׁ כֹּפֶר נַפְשׁוֹ (Shemos 30:12), a man's ransom for his soul, which he glosses as the removing of his soul's sin, that is, his redemption; so too אִם כֹּפֶר יוּשַׁת עָלָיו (Shemos 21:30), if a ransom is laid upon him.

וּכְפַר הָעַמֹּנָי (Yehoshua 18:24), and נָלִינָה בַּכְּפָרִים (Shir HaShirim 7:12), let us lodge in the villages. The Targum renders הָעִיר וּבְנוֹתֶיהָ, the city and its outlying towns, with וְכַפְרָנָהָא, its villages, which are houses outside the city, for villagers and for men who work the land.

אֶשְׁכֹּל הַכֹּפֶר (Shir HaShirim 1:14) he takes as a plant which he names by its Arabic name, and so כְּפָרִים עִם נְרָדִים (Shir HaShirim 4:13). Some hold that כְּפָרִים עִם נְרָדִים is a different spice and not the same thing. Ibn Ezra wrote that אֶשְׁכֹּל הַכֹּפֶר is the cluster of the date palm, since the palm carries different names as its season changes, and it has a season whose Arabic name is this one, and it has a good scent.

more.h: The young lion, the frost, the pans
more.t: כְּפִיר אֲרָיוֹת (Shoftim 14:5) and הַכְּפִירִים שֹׁאֲגִים לַטָּרֶף (Tehillim 104:21), the young lions roaring for prey: these are the young in days among the lions and the wild beasts, and a כְּפִיר is bigger than a גּוּר, a cub. By way of figure, כְּפִיר גּוֹיִם נִדְמֵיתָ (Yechezkel 32:2) means their great and mighty one. Apart from these, דַּק כַּכְּפֹר עַל הָאָרֶץ (Shemos 16:14), fine as the frost on the ground, which falls at daybreak in the cold days; and וְלִכְפוֹרֵי הַזָּהָב (Divrei HaYamim I 28:17), כַּפּוֹת זָהָב, pans of gold, which Chazal in Zevachim took as basins, named so because the knife is wiped clean of blood on them.

שֹער.sense: To dread, whence שְׂעָרָה, the storm; the שָׂעִיר, a he-goat, and the שְׂעִירִם; fine rain; hair, and a hairy man; and barley.

more.t: לֹא שְׂעָרוּם אֲבֹתֵיכֶם (Devarim 32:17) he reads as they did not dread them, that is, they did not fear them and did not serve them. The noun is the storm: בְּסוּפָה וּבִשְׂעָרָה דַּרְכּוֹ (Nachum 1:3), His way is in the whirlwind and in the storm.

שְׂעִיר עִזִּים (Bamidbar 7:16), a he-goat, is known. לַשְּׂעִירִם אֲשֶׁר הֵם זֹנִים אַחֲרֵיהֶם (Vayikra 17:7), the שְׂעִירִם after whom they stray, are the שֵׁדִים, the demons; they are called by this name because they are seen in the likeness of goats by those who believe in them.
כִּשְׂעִירִם עֲלֵי דֶשֶׁא (Devarim 32:2), which he glosses as the fine rain upon the grass.

more.h: Hair, the hairy man, and barley
more.t: שַׂעְרֵךְ כְּעֵדֶר הָעִזִּים (Shir HaShirim 4:1), your hair is like a flock of goats, which he reads as like the hair of a flock of goats; הֵן עֵשָׂו אָחִי אִישׁ שָׂעִר (Bereishis 27:11), Esav my brother is a hairy man; and וְהַפִּשְׁתָּה וְהַשְּׂעֹרָה (Shemos 9:31), the flax and the barley. The last two he calls known.

שׁער.sense: To reckon and estimate; שַׁעַר, a gate, and so the entrance of a whole land; and a second sense in שַׁעֲרוּרָה, which he leaves unglossed.

more.t: כְּמוֹ שָׁעַר בְּנַפְשׁוֹ כֶּן הוּא (Mishlei 23:7), as he reckons in his soul so is he; and in the plural מֵאָה שְׁעָרִים (Bereishis 26:12), a hundred measures, which he calls a matter of measure and estimate, and known. Some read שַׁעֲרוּרִיָּה in בְּבֵית יִשְׂרָאֵל רָאִיתִי (Hoshea 6:10), in the house of Yisrael I have seen, from this sense: what I reckoned of them I saw in them.

שַׁמָּה וְשַׁעֲרוּרָה (Yirmiyahu 5:30) and רָאִיתִי שַׁעֲרוּרָה (Yirmiyahu 23:14) he sets down as another sense without saying what it is, adding the form שַׁעֲרֻרִת (Yirmiyahu 18:13). Of כַּתְּאֵנִים הַשֹּׁעָרִים (Yirmiyahu 29:17), the foul figs, he does say what it is: an adjective, a matter of filth and foulness.

more.h: The gate, and the land's entrance
more.t: שַׁעַר הַשָּׁמָיִם (Bereishis 28:17), the gate of heaven, and from it the gatekeeper, שֹׁעֵר הָעִיר (Melachim II 7:10), the gatekeeper of the city. A whole land is called by its gate, after its entrance, as וְיִרַשׁ זַרְעֲךָ אֵת שַׁעַר אֹיְבָיו (Bereishis 22:17), your seed shall possess the gate of its enemies: a strong and fortified land is strong at its entrance, having mountains or seas about it, and once enemies have come in and passed those gates the whole land is taken before them. So פָּתוֹחַ נִפְתְּחוּ שַׁעֲרֵי אַרְצֵךְ (Nachum 3:13), the gates of your land are thrown wide open, and וְהֵצַר לְךָ בְּכָל שְׁעָרֶיךָ (Devarim 28:52), he will press you in all your gates.

קהל.sense: To gather, and to be gathered; the noun קָהָל, an assembly, with קְהִלָּה and מַקְהֵלִים for a gathering.

more.t: וַיִּקָּהֵל הָעָם עַל אַהֲרֹן (Shemos 32:1), the people gathered against Aharon, and הַנִּקְהָלִים עָלֶיךָ (Yechezkel 38:7), those gathered to you; where the verb takes an object, הַקְהֵל אֶת הָעָם (Devarim 31:12), assemble the people. The nouns are וְקָהָל וְעַם רָב (Yechezkel 26:7), an assembly and a great people, קְהִלַּת יַעֲקֹב (Devarim 33:4), the congregation of Yaakov, and בְּמַקְהֵלִים (Tehillim 26:12), in assemblies, with בְּמַקְהֵלוֹת (Tehillim 68:27) for the feminine plural.

In הַקָּהָל חֻקָּה אַחַת לָכֶם (Bamidbar 15:15) the heh is the heh of address, O assembly, one statute for you; the same heh as in הֶאָמוּר בֵּית יַעֲקֹב (Michah 2:7), O you who are called the house of Yaakov, and הַדּוֹר אַתֶּם רְאוּ (Yirmiyahu 2:31), O generation, see.

שׁמר.sense: To keep, to guard and to watch over; and by other senses the watches of the night, the lees of wine, שָׁמִיר, a hard stone, and שָׁמִיר, a thorn.

more.t: וְאָבִיו שָׁמַר אֶת הַדָּבָר (Bereishis 37:11), his father kept the matter, and וּשְׁמָרוֹ כְּרֹעֶה עֶדְרוֹ (Yirmiyahu 31:10), he will guard him as a shepherd guards his flock. It can also be a guarding that keeps others off: אֲנִי שָׁמַרְתִּי אָרְחוֹת פָּרִיץ (Tehillim 17:4) he reads as I watched the robber's paths so that no man should walk in them, and in the same way לִשְׁמֹר אֶת דֶּרֶךְ עֵץ הַחַיִּים (Bereishis 3:24).

וְרַק אַתֶּם שִׁמְרוּ מִן הַחֵרֶם (Yehoshua 6:18), only you, keep yourselves from the cherem: each man is to guard his fellow from it, for if one takes, all of them are punished, and that is why Yisrael were punished over Achan.

לֹא תִשְׁמוֹר עַל חַטָּאתִי (Iyov 14:16) can be that You watch only over my sin, the word carrying only, as אֵין טוֹב בָּאָדָם שֶׁיֹּאכַל (Koheles 2:24) means only that he eat; or that You will not wait, that is, You punish me at once and give me no time, as Chazal in Berachos say שמור לי על הפתח, wait for me at the door.

בְּאַשְׁמֹרֶת הַבֹּקֶר (Shemos 14:24), in the morning watch, and רֹאשׁ הָאַשְׁמֹרֶת הַתִּיכוֹנָה (Shoftim 7:19), the head of the middle watch; Chazal in Berachos say the night has three watches, and he holds that the pasuk in Shoftim bears it out. A city's watchman is named from this, since he is awake at night, guards the city and knows the hours. Of אָחַזְתָּ שְׁמֻרוֹת עֵינָי (Tehillim 77:5) he says it is as though You held the watches of my eyes so that they stay open and I do not sleep; Rabbi Moshe HaKohen takes שְׁמֻרוֹת in the first sense, as שׁוֹמְרוֹת, the eyelids that guard the eyes, which did not close.

וְשֹׁקֵט הוּא אֶל שְׁמָרָיו (Yirmiyahu 48:11), he rests on his lees, and הַקֹּפְאִים עַל שִׁמְרֵיהֶם (Tzefaniah 1:12), those congealed upon their lees. הִשָּׁמֵר וְהַשְׁקֵט (Yeshayahu 7:4) he reads here, settle on your lees in ease and quiet, and marks that it is accented on the last syllable, while everything in the sense of guarding is accented before it. Rav Saadiah Gaon read it instead as guarding: guard yourself from making war, and be quiet, do not fear.

more.h: שָׁמִיר, the hard stone and the thorn
more.t: כְּשָׁמִיר חָזָק מִצֹּר (Yechezkel 3:9), harder than flint, and מִצּוּר הַחַלָּמִישׁ (Devarim 8:15), which the Targum Yerushalmi renders שמרי טינרא, the shamir of the rock. Some read בְּצִפֹּרֶן שָׁמִיר (Yirmiyahu 17:1) as the hard iron, named so for its strength, as the hard rock is called שָׁמִיר. A second שָׁמִיר is a thorn: קוֹץ שָׁמִיר תַּעֲלֶה (Yeshayahu 32:13), which he reads as קוֹץ וְשָׁמִיר, thorn and brier, and שָׁמִיר וָשַׁיִת (Yeshayahu 9:17), a kind of thorn.

ארח.sense: אֹרַח, a way or path, and the verb taken from it; the wayfarer on it, the caravan that travels it, and a man's set meal.

more.t: וְאָרַח לְחֶבְרָה עִם פֹּעֲלֵי אָוֶן (Iyov 34:8), he keeps company with workers of iniquity, is the verb, and the noun it is taken from is אֹרַח, whose sense is דֶּרֶךְ, a way: וּכְאֹרַח אִישׁ יַמְצִאֶנּוּ (Iyov 34:11) and אָרְחִי וְרִבְעִי זֵרִיתָ (Tehillim 139:3). In the plural, חָדְלוּ אֳרָחוֹת (Shoftim 5:6) he glosses as those who pass along the ways ceased, and אֳרָחוֹת עֲקַלְקַלּוֹת stands in the same pasuk, crooked ways. On וְתִשְׁמוֹר כָּל אָרְחוֹתָי (Iyov 13:27), and You watch all my paths, he notes that Ben Asher reads it with a kamatz and Ben Naftali with a cholam.
לָאֹרֵחַ הַבָּא לוֹ (Shmuel II 12:4), the traveller who came to him: he is one going, עוֹבֵר אוֹרַח, passing along the way from place to place.
אֹרַח כַּנָּשִׁים (Bereishis 18:11) he glosses as the manner of women, and he brings כִּי דֶרֶךְ נָשִׁים לִי (Bereishis 31:35), for the way of women is upon me, as said in the same sense.

אֹרְחַת יִשְׁמְעֵאלִים (Bereishis 37:25), a caravan of Yishmaelim, which the Targum renders שְׁיָרַת עֲרָבָאֵי, a caravan of Arabians; so too אֹרְחוֹת דְּדָנִים (Yeshayahu 21:13). Because caravans are always going along the ways, they themselves were named for the ways.

וַאֲרֻחָתוֹ אֲרֻחַת תָּמִיד (Melachim II 25:30), which he glosses as his meal and his keep, and טוֹב אֲרֻחַת יָרָק (Mishlei 15:17), better a meal of herbs. These, he says, do not fall outside the first sense but are counted within it.

קדשׁ.sense: To be holy, and so to be set apart and forbidden to common use; and a second sense, to appoint or designate for a purpose.

more.t: פֶּן־ תִּקְדַּשׁ הַֽמְלֵאָה הַזֶּרַע (Devarim 22:9), lest the full yield of the seed be forfeit, he glosses as lest it become forbidden in benefit, the way what is consecrated is forbidden. Chazal in Kiddushin learn it from the same word in ואיש כי יקדיש את ביתו קדש, a man who consecrates his house: there the thing is forbidden in benefit, and so here.

וְאֶל־כָּל־מַֽאֲכָל הֲיִקְדָּשׁ (Chaggai 2:12) he glosses היטמא, will the food become tamei, forbidden by its tumah as consecrated food is forbidden; Chaggai was putting the laws of tumah to the kohanim, which they may have forgotten in the galus. Some of Chazal in Pesachim hold the kohanim erred in the answer, a fourth degree in kodesh being tamei; others that they erred in neither question; others that he asked about a fifth degree; others that he asked before a fourth degree in kodesh had been decreed. Radak holds the parsha shows they did not err, since throughout it he rebukes them over nothing but the building of the Beis.

כֹּל אֲשֶׁר־יִגַּע בִּבְשָׂרָהּ יִקְדָּשׁ (Vayikra 6:20): food that touches the flesh of the chatas and absorbs from it becomes holy as it is, and is eaten by whichever of the two laws is the stricter, so that shelamim flesh that touched a chatas is eaten for the chatas's day and night only. כָּל־הַנֹּגֵעַ בַּמִּזְבֵּחַ יִקְדָּֽשׁ (Shemos 29:37): even a korban already unfit that has gone up on the mizbeach is made fit by it, and once it has gone up it does not come down.

וְעָשׂוּ לִי מִקְדָּשׁ (Shemos 25:8), and they shall make Me a sanctuary; the house of holiness is the מִקְדָּשׁ. A king's palace is called so as well, כִּי מִקְדַּשׁ ־מֶלֶךְ הוּא (Amos 7:13), for it is like a mikdash, that none enter but those who are known there.

Some read מקדש at Yeshayahu 8:14 as a refuge, a place a man goes to be secure, and then לִשְׁנֵי בָתֵּי יִשְׂרָאֵל is one house for good and one for ill, Shevna and his party having made peace with the king of Ashur and Chizkiyahu and his party not. He offers another, that it is designation, a designation of punishment, a stumbling block set before them, as וְנָתַתִּי מִכְשׁוֹל לְפָנָיו (Yechezkel 3:20); on that reading the two houses are Pekach ben Remalyahu and Shevna's party, both of whom wanted the kingdom of Beis David to fall.

קַדְּשׁוּ ־צוֹם קִרְאוּ עֲצָרָה (Yoel 1:14), proclaim a fast, call an assembly, and קַדְּשׁוּ עָלֶיהָ מִלְחָמָה (Yirmiyahu 6:4), appoint war against her: these and their like are appointment. So too the קָדֵשׁ and the קְדֵשָׁה, לֹא־תִֽהְיֶה קְדֵשָׁה (Devarim 23:18), all of them being those appointed for lying with.

אמן.sense: To believe and to trust; and further, to be firm and enduring, to rear a child, and the אָמָּן, the master of a craft.

more.t: לְמַעַן יַֽאֲמִינוּ (Shemos 4:5), that they may believe. All such forms are trust and acceptance, קרידינצא in his own vernacular, credence; and they come out of אֱמוּנָה, since one who believes a thing gives it credence and holds it true.

In his own view אֱמֶת belongs to this root, its proper form being אֱמֶנֶת on the pattern of דְּבֶֽלֶת, the nun having fallen away for ease as it fell from בת, whose proper form is בֶּֽנֶת; the dagesh it takes when suffixes are joined to it proves as much, and its plural is formed as בנות is.

וְאָמַר כָּל־הָעָם אָמֵֽן (Devarim 27:17) is, it is true that whoever transgresses one of these shall be cursed, said either as a prayer or as acceptance, that they took the curse upon themselves should they transgress. So וְגַם־ אָמְנָה אֲחֹתִי בַת־אָבִי (Bereishis 20:12), it is true that she is my sister, my father's daughter.

A second strand of the root is standing firm. וְנֶֽאְמַן בֵּיתְךָ וּמַמְלַכְתְּךָ (Shmuel II 7:16), your house shall be established; יָתֵד בְּמָקוֹם נֶאֱמָן (Yeshayahu 22:23), a peg in a lasting place; מַכּוֹת גְּדֹלֹת וְנֶאֱמָנוֹת (Devarim 28:59), blows great and lasting; וַיְהִי יָדָיו אֱמוּנָה (Shemos 17:12), his hands held steady, and they did not let them down until the sun came in. אֲנַחְנוּ כֹּֽרְתִים אֲמָנָה (Nechemiah 10:1) is a binding covenant, and וְאֶת־ הָאֹמְנוֹת אֲשֶׁר צִפָּה חִזְקִיָּה (Melachim II 18:16) are the pillars that held the building up, which Yonasan renders וְיַת סְקוֹפַיָא, the thresholds of the gates.

כַּֽאֲשֶׁר יִשָּׂא הָֽאֹמֵן אֶת־הַיֹּנֵק (Bamidbar 11:12) is the one who rears him; וַתִּשָּׂאֵהוּ אֹֽמַנְתּוֹ (Shmuel II 4:4), his nurse; הָאֱמֻנִים עֲלֵי תוֹלָע (Eichah 4:5), those brought up on scarlet; וְאֶל־ הָאֹֽמְנִים אַחְאָב (Melachim II 10:1), those who reared him from his youth and were the men of his counsel, in whose charge the affairs of the kingdom lay. Here his father puts בָּנִים לֹֽא־ אֵמֻן בָּֽם (Devarim 32:21), that there is no breeding in them, a perverse generation who do evil when they are done good, as וַיִּשְׁמַן יְשֻׁרוּן וַיִּבְעָט (Devarim 32:15); Radak had taken those words above as children who do not believe, or in whom there is no truth.

more.h: Where he differs from Rabbi Yonah
more.t: Rabbi Yonah brought מֵסִיר שָׂפָה לְנֶאֱמָנִים (Iyov 12:20) into this root. Radak holds it is from נאם and of that sense, וַיִּנְֽאֲמוּ נְאֻֽם (Yirmiyahu 23:31), which is speaking, the closing nun added as the mark of an adjective, as in רחמן and נעמן; men clear in their tongue who know the wisdom of speech are called נאמנים.

שֹלם.sense: שַׂלְמָה, a garment: the letters of שִֹמְלָה turned about.

more.t: One line, on עַל־שֶׂה עַל־ שַׂלְמָה (Shemos 22:8), over a sheep, over a garment.

שׁלם.sense: To repay and requite; also to be complete and finished; and to be at peace, whence שָׁלוֹם.

more.t: יְשַׁלְּמוּנִי רָעָה תַּחַת טוֹבָה (Tehillim 35:12), they repay me evil for good; שַׁלֵּם יְשַׁלֵּם שׁוֹר תַּחַת הַשּׁוֹר (Shemos 21:36), he shall surely pay ox for ox. The nouns are בָּאוּ יְמֵי הַשִּׁלֻּם (Hoshea 9:7), the days of requital have come, וְשִׁלֻּמַת רְשָׁעִים תִּרְאֶֽה (Tehillim 91:8), and לִי נָקָם וְשִׁלֵּם (Devarim 32:35); all of them are recompense and payment.

כִּי לֹֽא־ שָׁלֵם עֲוֹן הָֽאֱמֹרִי עַד־הֵֽנָּה (Bereishis 15:16), the sin of the Emori is not yet full; וְשָֽׁלְמוּ יְמֵי אֶבְלֵֽךְ (Yeshayahu 60:20), the days of your mourning shall be ended; וַתִּשְׁלַם כָּל־הַמְּלָאכָה (Melachim I 7:51), all the work was finished. אֶבֶן שְׁלֵמָה (Devarim 25:15) is a full weight, and אֲבָנִים שְׁלֵמוֹת (Devarim 27:6) are whole stones that have not been cut. הָגְלָת שְׁלוֹמִֽים (Yirmiyahu 13:19) is that all of them went into exile, and on the same footing his father read מוּסַר שְׁלוֹמֵנוּ (Yeshayahu 53:5) as the chastisement of all of us.

שְֽׁלֵמִים הֵם אִתָּנוּ (Bereishis 34:21), they are at peace with us; הֲשָׁלוֹם אֲבִיכֶם הַזָּקֵן (Bereishis 43:27), is your aged father well. אִם־גָּמַלְתִּי שׁוֹלְמִי רָע (Tehillim 7:5) is, did I repay evil to one who was at peace with me. Where the verb takes an object it is to make peace: כִּֽי־ הִשְׁלִימָה אֶת־יְהוֹשֻׁעַ (Yehoshua 10:4), and גַּם־אוֹיְבָיו יַשְׁלִם אִתּֽוֹ (Mishlei 16:7), He makes even a man's enemies to be at peace with him.

more.h: Why the שְׁלָמִים is so called
more.t: Of the עולה everything goes up whole and the hide to the kohanim; of the chatas and the asham the blood and the eimurim go to the mizbeach and the breast and thigh to the kohanim; but of זֶבַח שְׁלָמִים (Vayikra 3:1) the blood and the eimurim go to the mizbeach, the breast and thigh to the kohanim, and the rest of the flesh and the hide to the owners, so that this zevach is peace between them all, as the Sifra sets it out. For the same reason it is called מִלּוּאִים, כִּי אֵיל מִלֻּאִים הֽוּא (Shemos 29:22), because it filled the desire of all of them, all of them eating from it.
שׁוּבִי שׁוּבִי הַשּׁוּלַמִּית (Shir HaShirim 7:1) is she who dwells in Yerushalayim, which is called שָׁלֵם.

ראה.sense: To see, and so to perceive and understand; with מַרְאֶה, a sight or a vision, and רֹאֶה, the one who sees, the navi.

more.t: וְלִבִּי רָאָה הַרְבֵּה חָכְמָה וָדָֽעַת (Koheles 1:16), my heart saw much wisdom and knowledge. So וַיַּרְא יַֽעֲקֹב כִּי יֶשׁ־שֶׁבֶר (Bereishis 42:1): he saw that the people of the land were going to Mitzrayim to buy grain, or he saw in his heart, that is, he understood from what he had heard and seen. הַדּוֹר אַתֶּם רְאוּ (Yirmiyahu 2:31) is, give your mind to the word of Hashem, and רְאֵה דְבָרֶיךָ טוֹבִים וּנְכֹחִים (Shmuel II 15:3) is, give your mind and understand.

more.h: The other senses lent to sight
more.t: Because the eye's perception is greater than the rest, the other senses are spoken of as seeing: וְכָל־הָעָם רֹאִים אֶת־הַקּוֹלֹת (Shemos 20:18), all the people saw the sounds, and רְאֵה רֵיחַ בְּנִי (Bereishis 27:27), see the smell of my son.

שָׁגוּ בָּֽרֹאֶה (Yeshayahu 28:7) he takes as, they erred in prophecy; his father read it as, they erred in a thing plain to every man. Rabbi Yaakov ben Elazar wrote that רואה is a noun of seeing and that אַֽחֲרֵי רֹאִֽי (Bereishis 16:13) is after my prophecy, and Radak says it is right; earlier in the entry he had read those words of the One seen by him, who saw him in his affliction.

לֹֽא־ אֶרְאֶה (Yeshayahu 38:11) Rav Saadiah Gaon explained in the sense of thanksgiving, and Radak says it is right, since to see the Creator is to give thanks and praise before Him and to consider His ways.

Some read הֵמָּה יַבִּיטוּ יִרְאוּ ־בִֽי (Tehillim 22:18), they look, they stare at me, as contempt, and so לְרַֽאֲוָה בָֽךְ (Yechezkel 28:17). He holds there is no need to take them out of their own sense, and brings Targum Yonasan, who renders לְרַֽאֲוָה בָֽךְ as לְאִסְתַכְּלָא בָךְ, to look at you.

וְהֵסִיר אֶת־ מֻרְאָתוֹ בְּנֹֽצָתָהּ (Vayikra 1:16) is the bird's crop, as the Targum has it; וְשַׂמְתִּיךְ כְּרֹֽאִי (Nachum 3:6) is filth and defilement. Of וְהָֽרָאָה וְאֶת־הָאַיָּה (Devarim 14:13) Chazal in Chullin say that רָאָה is דָּאָה, and that it is named רָאָה because it sees further than others.

עלה.sense: To go up and to rise; by a second sense, to be cut off and to cease; and from it עֹלָה, the offering that goes up whole, עֲלִיָּה, an upper room, and עָלֶה, a leaf.

more.t: עָלִיתָ לַמָּרוֹם (Tehillim 68:19), You went up on high; וְעָלָה הַגְּבוּל (Yehoshua 15:8), the border goes up; וּבָשָׂר עָלָה (Yechezkel 37:8), flesh came up over the sinews and the bones; כִּי עָלָה הַשָּׁחַר (Bereishis 32:26), the brightness of the day has come up. מִֽלְמַֽעֲלֵה הֶחָֽרֶס (Shoftim 8:13) he reads as the rising of the sun's brightness; Targum Yonasan has עַד לָא מֵעַל שִׁמְשָׁא, before the sun set, and on that reading the word means while the sun was still up, seen in the sky and not yet gone under the earth.

עֹלָה הוּא אִשֵּׁה רֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ (Vayikra 1:13). The korban is called so because it went up whole upon the mizbeach. שֹׂנֵא גָזֵל בְּעוֹלָה (Yeshayahu 61:8) is, if a man brings before Me an olah that was stolen I hate it, as וַֽהֲבֵאתֶם גָּזוּל (Malachi 1:13).

more.h: The other sense, being cut off
more.t: יְצוּעִי עָלָֽה (Bereishis 49:4), from the day you profaned it my couch was cut off; שֻׁדַּד מוֹאָב וְעָרֶיהָ עָלָה (Yirmiyahu 48:15); וַתַּעַל שִׁכְבַת הַטָּל (Shemos 16:14); אַֽל־ תַּֽעֲלֵנִי בַּֽחֲצִי יָמָי (Tehillim 102:25), do not cut me off in the midst of my days. Some read וְעָֽלְתָה יָדוֹ עַל־יַד רֵעֵֽהוּ (Zechariah 14:13) so, that the hand is torn away, and Targum Yonasan has וְתִתְּלַשׁ יְדֵיהּ. Some read וְהַבַּיִת הַזֶּה יִֽהְיֶה עֶלְיוֹן (Melachim I 9:8) of cutting off and ruin too; he holds there is no need to take it out of the first sense, and reads it as, this house which is now high, when they sin every passer by will be appalled and hiss.

more.h: Rooms above, steps, and the hours
more.t: וַיָּסַר אֶל־ הָֽעֲלִיָּה (Melachim II 4:11) and עֲלִיַּת ־קִיר (Melachim II 4:10) are the upper chamber, so called because it is over the house and a man goes up to it, and וְלֹא־תַֽעֲלֶה בְמַֽעֲלֹת (Shemos 20:23) are steps, because a man goes up on them. צֵל הַֽמַּֽעֲלוֹת (Yeshayahu 38:8) Targum Yonasan renders טוּל אֶבֶן שְׁעַיָא, which is the אבן השעות of the Mishnah in Keilim, the stone marked so as to know the hours of the day.

He writes עַל under this root, from the first sense: עֲלֵֽי ־עָשׂוֹר וַֽעֲלֵי ־נָבֶל (Tehillim 92:4), and without the yud of the plural עַל ־פְּנֵי הַמָּֽיִם (Bereishis 1:2). It comes in the sense of with: וַיָּבֹאוּ הָֽאֲנָשִׁים עַל ־הַנָּשִׁים (Shemos 35:22), the men came with the women. It comes in the sense of beside: וְזָֽבַחְתָּ עָלָיו אֶת־עֹֽלֹתֶיךָ (Shemos 20:21), beside it, for he did not slaughter upon the mizbeach, and חֹנִים עַל ־הַיָּם (Shemos 14:9), by the sea. It stands for אל: וַיֵּלֶךְ אֶלְקָנָה הָֽרָמָתָה עַל ־בֵּיתוֹ (Shmuel I 2:11), to his house; and for the letter beis: הִמָּלֵט עַל ־נַפְשֶׁךָ (Bereishis 19:17), which he reads as בנפשך, with your life.

וְהִנֵּה עֲלֵה ־זַיִת טָרָף בְּפִיהָ (Bereishis 8:11) and וַֽיִּתְפְּרוּ עֲלֵה תְאֵנָה (Bereishis 3:7) are the leaf; of וְהָבִיאוּ עֲלֵי ־זַיִת (Nechemiah 8:15) he says the branches together with the leaves are meant. His father read הִצִּית אֵשׁ עָלֶיהָ (Yirmiyahu 11:16) as on its leaves, and Dunash read פֶּן יִפְקֹד עָלֶיהָ (Yeshayahu 27:3) from this, that not even the leaf should be missing, still less the fruit.
